Accurate dynamics, continuous visibility, and sparse views

The corrected six-substep integrator has about 0.130 mm coordinate RMSE against independent RK4-96, versus about 3.3 mm for historical Euler-3. Smooth overlapping depth integration replaces whole-splat depth sorting. This is numerical validation on two known-scene toy sequences, not real-world physical validation.

Numerical checks

Halving the staggered time step reduces deterministic position error by about four. Its parameter-dependent density determinant is included so force marginalization remains normalized. Production 128-slab rendering differs from 1024 slabs by about 2.15e-5 RGB RMSE, and the 512-slab image reference by about 1.0e-6; observation noise SD is 0.015.

The 0.130 mm figure is a coordinate average: the maximum node/time error is about 0.626 mm. At twelve substeps the corresponding values are about 0.032 mm and 0.156 mm. The fixed production fit uses six substeps; these checks do not establish full posterior convergence under time refinement or mesh refinement.

Actual images

Images are 24 x 24 pixels. Native tiles are enlarged without inventing detail. Display clips noisy RGB to [0,1]; fitting uses unclipped values. Reference images are re-rendered from RK4-96 positions using the new continuous renderer. Original six-view noise residuals are reused. All controls see the same new images.

Three solvers under the corrected model

All solvers share the same initialization, force prior, discrepancy model, corrected discretization and renderer. The budget is 20 iterations. 4/6 primary corrected fits pass the common marginal stationarity screen; 4/6 pass the independent local-Gaussian importance-weight screen. A passed screen is not posterior calibration. Force elimination is exact conditional on trajectory; trajectory inference remains a local approximation.

Position RMSE averages squared errors over the twelve free-node coordinates and the named times, then takes a square root. Pinned nodes are excluded. Local interval coverage counts correlated components from these two sequences, not independent calibration replicates. Fit times include final covariance construction and are single CPU-run measurements.

Scope and handover

Two deterministic sequences, one tiny 8-node/6-tetrahedron mesh, fixed force profile and one noise realization. Geometry, appearance, density, supports and camera poses are known. No real video, unknown-geometry completion, arbitrary force location, mesh convergence, contact, or calibrated uncertainty is established. The stochastic reference remains uncertified. The renderer is a continuous projected-footprint volume surrogate, not exact 3D Gaussian ray tracing. Stored staggered velocities produce finite-difference integer-time estimates rather than exact SDE velocities.

The force prior is a finite five-knot Matérn inducing projection, not an unrestricted GP. Its temporal basis need not reproduce the analytic narrow pulse exactly. An evaluation-only dense-grid oracle projection is saved in force_basis_audit.json; it never initializes or tunes a fit.

Compact inputs, fitted solver coordinates, point paths, force distributions, records and source/environment provenance accompany this offline report. Full raw precisions remain in ignored local checkpoints and can be regenerated from the committed plan. Historical results have not been overwritten.
